fields.Name: N1r -> S6.5
fields.Description: Gate G2.2 (phase 2, dataset N1r, criterion S6.5): over 400 N1r seeds, the gate returns outcome `model` in ≤ 28 publications of 400 (same rule); the reference's outcome is no-signal. A statistical gate: the pytest node tests/gates/test_seeds400.py::test_N1r_S6_5_noise_publish trains one run per seed through the trainer and counts the sidecar's gate outcomes; the stored outcome is the engine's decision over the same intervals plus guards that only demote model, and a run whose sidecar decision differs is refused, so the sidecar's model count bounds the stored count. PS_SEED_LIMIT=<k> runs the first k seeds with the cap scaled to k (floor of 28k/400); the full count runs once, on the final head. The node is Python, so the mutation is a substitute: it fails when the sidecar gate (app/gate.py run_gate) tests the point estimate instead of the interval's lower bound on the model's comparisons (modelVsDummy and modelVs:<member>; publications above the bound, run at 40 seeds). Applied to every comparison, the point estimate also makes the simple members eligible and the gate keeps a baseline instead of publishing (measured at 40 seeds: 0, 0 and 1 model outcomes on N1c, N1r and W2-noise, within the cap of 2), so it cannot fail a noise-publication gate; the TypeScript GateRules.BeatsByMargin mutation is caught by the gate parity tests (test_gate_inputs_from_intervals_matches_reference).

ExpectedOutcomes.summary: Over N1r's n400 set (400 seeds) the gate returns model in at most 28 (1 of 1 pytest case).
